title: How I Reached Home
question: Can he bring what he saw back into his own house?

flight.described: the open heather of Horsell Common at night in 1894, away from the pit: knee-deep purple-brown heather and dark furze standing black in every direction, young Scots pines in loose stands with bare trunks, bare sand tracks worn pale through the heather, the ground broken and uneven underfoot, a horizon that runs dead flat and level, closed by a line of low pines, and a low red glow in the sky behind on that horizon where the pit lies; the only light is that glow from behind, low and raking, so the heather reads black and the pine trunks catch a dull red down one side
flight.landmark: the low red glow in the sky behind on the horizon
flight.landmark_size: is a twelfth of the height of the frame
flight.route: from out among the pines on the black common down toward the road
flight.geometry: Black heather fills the BOTTOM two thirds of the frame from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge. The nearest pine trunk stands at the LEFT third from the BOTTOM to the TOP third, its bark clearly lit red down the side that faces the glow and rough enough to read. A bare sand track runs from the BOTTOM CENTRE away into the CENTRE, pale and clearly lit against the black heather on both sides of it. Further trunks stand at the RIGHT third, a flat line of low pines closes the horizon across the CENTRE, and a low red glow lies along it under a black sky that fills the TOP third.

canal.described: the bridge that carries the road over the canal by the Woking gasworks at night in 1894: a low brick humpback bridge with a stone parapet, the black canal water below it, the tarred gasworks retort house and its two gasholders standing beyond, a grass verge and a milestone at the roadside, and a row of electric lamps burning along the works wall; the light is that lamp light from the right, hard and white, so the road and the parapet read pale grey, the water reads black, and everything away from the lamps is black
canal.landmark: the lit gasholders of the gasworks beyond the bridge
canal.landmark_size: is a third of the height of the frame
canal.route: from the grass verge at the roadside up over the hump of the canal bridge
canal.geometry: The pale road runs from the BOTTOM edge up over the hump of the bridge at the CENTRE and away. The stone parapet runs across the CENTRE from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge. Black canal water shows at the BOTTOM LEFT below it, the gasholders stand at the RIGHT third against the TOP third, and a line of hard white lamps burns along the RIGHT edge.

arch.described: the road up Maybury Hill at night in 1894 where it passes under the railway arch: a brick railway arch across the road with the embankment above it, a pretty row of gabled brick villas called Oriental Terrace along the near side each with a low front gate and a strip of garden, lit windows and a gas street lamp at the kerb, and the hill going up dark beyond; the light is gaslight from the left and the lit windows behind it, warm and low, so the road reads pale, the gables read warm brick and the arch and the embankment are black

shots.turn: a man carrying the news -> a man carrying a story
shots.why: All three of them laughed.

shots.frame: Medium close on the narrator, a slender narrow-shouldered man of thirty-four with a long oval face, grey eyes and dark brown hair parted on the left, a neat close-trimmed dark brown moustache and shaven cheeks, in a mid-grey herringbone tweed suit with the jacket torn at the left elbow, his starched collar sprung from its stud and his green tie pulled sideways, bareheaded at the gate at night with the laughter going on in front of him, his mouth half open on a sentence he has given up, his hand coming down off the railings.
shots.motion: The camera holds a static shot level with his face; his mouth closes after the words; his hand comes down off the railings and goes on down to his side; he turns his shoulder away from the gate and goes on turning until the light leaves his face.
shots.camera: on the pavement level with his face, two paces from him, a 50mm lens. The window light comes from the LEFT and lights one side of his face; the road behind him is black
shots.at_rest: The narrator's head and shoulders fill the CENTRE of the frame, the panel cutting him at the middle of the chest, his head a third the frame's height at the TOP third. The iron railings cross the BOTTOM third and the black road fills the frame behind him.
shots.why: I tried and found I could not tell them what I had seen.

shots.frame: Medium on the narrator's wife, a slim straight-backed woman of twenty-nine with an oval face, wide hazel eyes and light freckles across the nose, her thick chestnut-auburn hair swept up into a soft pompadour, in a lilac-grey cotton house dress with a high collar and a white bibbed apron tied at the waist, a plain gold band on her hand standing in her own lit doorway at night with the door held open against her shoulder, the warm hall light behind her, looking out at something on the step that has stopped her where she stands.
shots.motion: The camera rises from the step with small amplitude until her face and the lit hall behind her are both in the picture, travelling one short stride; her hand goes on tightening on the edge of the door; the hall light goes on falling out across the step past her.
shots.camera: on the doorstep level with her face, three paces from her, a 50mm lens. The hall light comes from behind her and rims her hair and shoulder; her face reads dim and the garden behind the camera is black
shots.at_rest: The brick railway arch crosses the CENTRE of the frame from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge, black, with the embankment above it filling the TOP third. The pale road runs from the BOTTOM edge through the arch at the CENTRE. The gabled villas of Oriental Terrace stand along the LEFT from the BOTTOM LEFT to the CENTRE with lit windows, and a gas lamp stands at the kerb at the CENTRE LEFT.
shots.why: I startled my wife at the doorway, so haggard was I.

shots.frame: Insert on a burst collar stud and an open shirt collar at night, close: the linen collar sprung away from its fastener at the throat, the brass stud hanging by its shank, and a smear of sand and heather dust across the linen, with warm hall light falling across it from one side.
shots.motion: The camera holds a static shot close on the collar; the loose stud goes on swinging a little on its shank; the warm light goes on moving across the linen as the door behind swings.
shots.camera: on the doorstep close to his throat, a 50mm lens. The hall light comes from the LEFT and rakes the linen; the collar reads warm white and everything behind it is black
shots.at_rest: The brick railway arch crosses the CENTRE of the frame from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge, black, with the embankment above it filling the TOP third. The pale road runs from the BOTTOM edge through the arch at the CENTRE. The gabled villas of Oriental Terrace stand along the LEFT from the BOTTOM LEFT to the CENTRE with lit windows, and a gas lamp stands at the kerb at the CENTRE LEFT.
shots.why: A decent ordinary citizen, with the common still on him.

shots.frame: Wide of the little dining room at night, the two chairs at the table both empty: a mahogany table laid with a white cloth, a cold joint and bread and a decanter of wine set out, two chairs drawn up, an oil lamp burning in the middle of the cloth and the corners of the room black.
shots.motion: The camera rises from the table with small amplitude until the whole laid cloth and the papered wall behind it stand inside the picture, travelling one short stride; the lamp flame leans and rights itself as the door behind opens; the light goes on moving on the cloth.
shots.camera: at the end of the table a little above it, a 35mm lens. The oil lamp on the table is the only light and it comes from below; the cloth reads warm white and the corners of the room are black
shots.at_rest: The laid table fills the BOTTOM half of the frame from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge, its white cloth the brightest thing in the picture. The oil lamp stands at the CENTRE on the table, the cold joint and the decanter at the CENTRE RIGHT, and the papered wall with its framed landscape print fills the TOP third behind, going black at the LEFT edge and the RIGHT edge.
shots.turn: a house that has not heard -> a house that has
shots.why: The dinner, a cold one, had already been served.

shots.frame: Medium on the narrator, a slender narrow-shouldered man of thirty-four with a long oval face, grey eyes and dark brown hair parted on the left, a neat close-trimmed dark brown moustache and shaven cheeks, in a mid-grey herringbone tweed suit with the jacket torn at the left elbow, his starched collar sprung from its stud and his green tie pulled sideways, bareheaded sitting at the laid table at night with a glass of wine in his hand, his collar still open, talking steadily across the cloth with the lamp between him and the camera.
shots.motion: The camera holds a static shot across the table level with his chest; he sets the glass down on the cloth and leaves his hand round it; he goes on talking with his eyes on the lamp between them.
shots.camera: across the table level with his chest, four paces from him, a 50mm lens. The oil lamp is between them and lights him from below; the wall behind him is black
shots.at_rest: The laid table fills the BOTTOM half of the frame from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge, its white cloth the brightest thing in the picture. The oil lamp stands at the CENTRE on the table, the cold joint and the decanter at the CENTRE RIGHT, and the papered wall with its framed landscape print fills the TOP third behind, going black at the LEFT edge and the RIGHT edge.
shots.why: They may keep the pit and kill people who come near them.

shots.frame: Insert on the cold dinner standing whole on the white cloth at night: a cut joint on its dish with the fat set hard and grey, a cottage loaf beside it, two clean plates and a decanter with the light of the lamp standing in the wine, and the knives and forks square where they were laid.
shots.motion: The camera holds a static shot close over the cloth; the light in the decanter goes on shifting as the lamp flame moves; a bead of condensation goes on running down the glass.
shots.camera: over the table close to the cloth, a 50mm lens. The oil lamp is beside it and lights it from the side; the cloth reads warm white and the room beyond is black
shots.at_rest: The laid table fills the BOTTOM half of the frame from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge, its white cloth the brightest thing in the picture. The oil lamp stands at the CENTRE on the table, the cold joint and the decanter at the CENTRE RIGHT, and the papered wall with its framed landscape print fills the TOP third behind, going black at the LEFT edge and the RIGHT edge.
shots.why: It remained neglected on the table while I told my story.

shots.frame: Medium close over the shoulder of the wife toward the narrator, a slender narrow-shouldered man of thirty-four with a long oval face, grey eyes and dark brown hair parted on the left, a neat close-trimmed dark brown moustache and shaven cheeks, in a mid-grey herringbone tweed suit with the jacket torn at the left elbow, his starched collar sprung from its stud and his green tie pulled sideways, bareheaded at the table at night: the back of her head and her pale shoulder near and soft at the LEFT, turned away so only her hair shows, the narrator square in the right of the picture with the decanter at his elbow, explaining something reasonable to her across the cloth.
shots.motion: The camera holds a static shot over her shoulder, keeping his face in the right of frame; he lifts the decanter and goes on pouring for her; his other hand goes on turning over as he explains.
shots.camera: across the table level with their eyes, two paces behind her, a 50mm lens. The oil lamp lights his face from below at the LEFT; her shoulder in the near left is soft and dim
shots.at_rest: The BACK of the wife's head and her shoulder fill the LEFT third of the frame from the TOP edge to the BOTTOM edge, turned fully away from the camera, soft and out of focus. The narrator sits at the RIGHT third, the panel cutting him at the middle of the chest, his head a third the frame's height at the TOP third. The white cloth crosses the BOTTOM third between them.
shots.why: I pressed her to take wine, and tried to reassure her.

shots.frame: Insert on the oil lamp standing on the white cloth at night, close: its brass reservoir and glass chimney with the flame standing straight up inside, the cloth around its foot bright, and the black of the room beginning a hand's breadth beyond the light.
shots.motion: The camera holds a static shot close on the chimney; the flame leans over and comes straight again as something moves in the room; the ring of light on the cloth goes on breathing in and out with it.
shots.camera: on the table close to the lamp, a 50mm lens. The lamp is the light and it comes from the CENTRE; the cloth reads warm white and everything a hand's breadth beyond it is black
shots.at_rest: The laid table fills the BOTTOM half of the frame from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge, its white cloth the brightest thing in the picture. The oil lamp stands at the CENTRE on the table, the cold joint and the decanter at the CENTRE RIGHT, and the papered wall with its framed landscape print fills the TOP third behind, going black at the LEFT edge and the RIGHT edge.
shots.why: The last light in the house, and how far it reaches.

shots.frame: Medium close on the narrator's wife, a slim straight-backed woman of twenty-nine with an oval face, wide hazel eyes and light freckles across the nose, her thick chestnut-auburn hair swept up into a soft pompadour, in a lilac-grey cotton house dress with a high collar and a white bibbed apron tied at the waist, a plain gold band on her hand at the table at night, her face deadly white in the lamplight, her brows knitted and her hand laid flat on the cloth halfway across it toward him, listening with her plate still square in front of her.
shots.motion: The camera tilts up from the cloth to her face, travelling a hand's breadth, until her eyes are in the middle of the picture; her hand goes on further across the cloth toward his; the lamplight goes on moving on her face as the flame works.
shots.camera: across the table level with her face, three paces from her, a 50mm lens. The oil lamp lights her from below and from the LEFT; her face reads warm white and the room behind her is black
shots.at_rest: The wife's head and shoulders fill the CENTRE of the frame, the panel cutting her at the middle of the chest, her head a third the frame's height at the TOP third. The white cloth fills the BOTTOM third with her hand laid flat on it. The papered wall of the dining room stands behind her with its framed landscape print at the RIGHT third and the curtained sash window at the LEFT third, both dim in the lamplight, so the room she is sitting in is visible all round her.
shots.turn: a wife being reassured -> a wife who is right
shots.why: They may come here. She says it again and again, and she is right.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Of the running I kept nothing. Trees, and the shock of hitting them.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Everything I could not see was them, and it was all around me.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Somewhere above, I was sure, that blade of heat was still turning.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: At last I could go no further, and I fell by the wayside.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Then the ground had me, and I stayed on it a long while.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Did that happen? Did any of that happen?

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Somewhere behind me was my hat. My collar had torn off its stud.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The fear came off me like a garment, and I was a citizen again.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The heath, the quiet, the flames going up: a dream I had just left.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: A head rose over the arch, and a workman with a basket came by.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: He wished me good night. I made a noise at him and walked on.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Over the Maybury arch a train went flying south, and it had gone.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: All of it ordinary, all of it certain. And two miles back, that.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Three of them stood talking at a front gate, and I stopped there.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: What news from the common?

lines.speaker: unnamed_neighbour
lines.text: Ain't yer just been there?

lines.speaker: unnamed_neighbours_wife
lines.text: People seem fair silly about the common. What's it all about?

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Haven't you heard of the men from Mars, I said. The creatures from Mars.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: You'll hear more yet.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I felt foolish, and went on home.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: My wife opened the door. She stepped back from the look of me.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: The collar had gone at the stud. I never felt it go.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I went in, sat down, drank some wine, and told her what I had seen.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: Nothing alive has ever moved so slowly, I told her. They barely crawl.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: They may keep the pit, but they cannot get out of it.

lines.speaker: unnamed_first_person_narrator
lines.text: I laid stress on the weight of them here, and overlooked two things.

lines.speaker: narrators_wife
lines.text: They may come here.
